samples.summary: Large untrusted-clipboard hardening bundled into a heading-memory bug fix (scope creep)
samples.evidence: The stated change is the bulleted-heading round trip (#783: `unlistedBlockType`, split/merge/paste memory rules). Alongside it the diff adds ~300 lines of new clipboard payload validation (`sanitizeBlock*`, `asStoredColor`, `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`, `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH`, id regeneration, table-depth caps) plus a defensive clamp in `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:96-102). That is a distinct trust-boundary/security concern with its own behavioural contract (pasted block ids are now regenerated, unknown fields dropped, colSpan/rowSpan/columnWidths coerced), not required by the heading-memory outcome — the heading fix only needs `headingLevel` narrowing. Bundling it makes the PR hard to review and couples two unrelated risks; it belongs in its own change with its own design entry.

samples.summary: Clipboard payload contract change documented in docs.md instead of the canonical clipboard/copy-paste design doc; docs-table-copy-paste.md not updated
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-copy-paste.md:51,62,72,199` is the canonical record of the `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` payload (`serializeClipboard`/`deserializeClipboard`, `tableCells`). This change alters that payload's contract (values shape-checked, unknown keys dropped, block ids regenerated, colSpan/rowSpan truncated, columnWidths defaulted to 100, nesting capped at 8), yet the new prose lands in the 'Empty list-item Backspace exits the list' section of docs/design/docs/docs.md and the copy-paste doc is untouched. Per the repo's 'fold into the canonical subsystem doc' rule, the clipboard trust boundary belongs there (or in docs-context-menu.md's paste section), not under a Backspace heading.
searchedFor: glob docs/design/**/*.md for a clipboard/paste doc

samples.summary: Heading memory modelled as an inert field on `list-item`, forcing special cases across split/merge/paste/CRDT; an orthogonal list attribute on the heading block would fit the existing model better
samples.evidence: `Block` already carries `listKind`/`listLevel` as independent optional fields (types.ts:63-64); only the `type === 'list-item'` discriminator forces a heading to lose its identity when bulleted. Choosing to keep an inert `headingLevel` on `list-item` instead required new provenance predicates in three layers — `splitMovesHeadingMemory`/`mergeDropsHeadingMemory` (store/block-helpers.ts), `foldedHeadingLevel` (view/text-editor.ts:47-59), duplicated `removeStyleByPath` handling in `YorkieDocStore.splitBlock`/`mergeBlock`, plus a clipboard rule. That is a lot of cross-layer coupling for a field that changes nothing observable while set; the Google Docs model the doc cites treats the list as a paragraph property orthogonal to the named style.

samples.summary: Restore-on-unlist only covers `heading`; bulleting a Title/Subtitle still flattens to a paragraph, so the stated parity rule is applied inconsistently
samples.evidence: `unlistedBlockType` returns `{type:'heading'}` only when `block.headingLevel !== undefined`, else `'paragraph'`. `BlockType` also has `'title'` and `'subtitle'` (types.ts:39), which `blockStyleId` treats as first-class named styles (model/named-styles.ts:101-104). Bulleting a Title and un-bulleting it still yields body text, so the 'bullet is applied *to* the style' rule the design doc states (docs/design/docs/docs.md:117-134) holds for headings only, with no note of the gap.

samples.summary: 'Google Docs / Word parity' claim overstated: while bulleted, the heading is fully demoted (style id normal, no DOCX Heading style, no PDF outline entry)
samples.evidence: The doc claims parity because 'bulleting a heading applies the bullet *to* the heading', but the same paragraph says the level is inert and every reader gates on `type === 'heading'`; the new tests assert exactly that (packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts: markdown emits '- Quarterly results', `blockStyleId` is 'normal', DOCX emits no `w:pStyle w:val="Heading"`, and packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/text-style-options.test.ts asserts the toolbar reads 'Normal text'). In Google Docs a bulleted Heading 2 keeps its heading formatting, outline entry and export style. The change delivers only the un-bullet round trip; the doc should scope the parity claim to that rather than to the rendered/exported result.

samples.summary: Paste's provenance rule (`foldedHeadingLevel`) lives in text-editor.ts while its siblings live in store/block-helpers.ts and are exported from both entries
samples.evidence: `splitMovesHeadingMemory` and `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` were added to `packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts` and re-exported from `src/index.ts` and `src/node.ts` precisely so both the memory store and `YorkieDocStore` share them, but the third instance of the same rule (`foldedHeadingLevel`) is a private helper in the view layer, so any other paste/fold path (e.g. text-box editor, slides) cannot reuse it and will drift.

finding.summary: Large untrusted-clipboard hardening bundled into a heading-memory bug fix (scope creep)
finding.evidence: The stated change is the bulleted-heading round trip (#783: `unlistedBlockType`, split/merge/paste memory rules). Alongside it the diff adds ~300 lines of new clipboard payload validation (`sanitizeBlock*`, `asStoredColor`, `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`, `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH`, id regeneration, table-depth caps) plus a defensive clamp in `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:96-102). That is a distinct trust-boundary/security concern with its own behavioural contract (pasted block ids are now regenerated, unknown fields dropped, colSpan/rowSpan/columnWidths coerced), not required by the heading-memory outcome — the heading fix only needs `headingLevel` narrowing. Bundling it makes the PR hard to review and couples two unrelated risks; it belongs in its own change with its own design entry.

verdict.reason: The clipboard-sanitization code and the docx clamp do exist (clipboard.ts:32-332, docx-style-map.ts:95-103), but the finding's blocking rationale is contradicted by the repo. docs/design/docs/docs.md:225-235 — inside the canonical Docs subsystem design doc, added by this change (it cites the new mergeDropsHeadingMemory/foldedHeadingLevel helpers) — explicitly derives the hardening from the heading-memory rule: because a list-item's remembered headingLevel now travels through the paste path, the attacker-controllable application/x-waffledocs payload becomes a vector into the Yorkie tree and into buildParagraphPropertiesXml's <w:pStyle> interpolation. So the work is neither undocumented nor filed as a parallel doc, and it is not the "unrelated risk" the finding claims. No acceptance criterion of the originating task is unmet (all steps in docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:34-47 are implemented) and none of its stated Non-goals (lines 49-58) is exceeded; no existing module is duplicated (only clipboard.ts validates this MIME payload). What is left is "should have been split into a separate PR / easier to review" — a preference, which this lens's rubric classifies as minor/nit and states never blocks.

finding.summary: `splitMovesHeadingMemory` (offset-0 split moves the remembered level) contradicts the plan's stated Non-goal on splitting
finding.evidence: The spec's Non-goals say: "Splitting a bulleted heading (Enter) — the new item stays a plain list item, as today. ... `applySplitBlock` keeps dropping `headingLevel` for a non-`heading` split half. Only the block that was actually bulleted remembers." The diff introduces an exception (offset 0 moves the memory), and to honour it adds a shared predicate plus new CRDT writes in `YorkieDocStore.splitBlock` (`removeStyleByPath(['headingLevel'])` and stamping the attr onto the new node) — new collaborative-edit surface not covered by the plan. Either the plan's Non-goal should be amended explicitly, or this exception belongs in a follow-up; as written the diff both asserts the Non-goal (docs.md) and carves an exception into it.

verdict.reason: Every element of the presence claim checks out in the working tree. `splitMovesHeadingMemory` exists (block-helpers.ts:290-302) and makes an offset-0 split MOVE a bulleted heading's remembered level: `applySplitBlock` keeps it on the new half and deletes it from the original (block-helpers.ts:260-266). To keep the CRDT in sync, `YorkieDocStore.splitBlock` adds new collaborative writes — `tree.removeStyleByPath(blockPath, endPath, ['headingLevel'])` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2030) and `afterAttrs.headingLevel` stamping when `movesHeadingMemory` (2062-2067). Meanwhile the originating task plan still states the opposite as a Non-goal: docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:53-57 ("the new item stays a plain list item, as today … `applySplitBlock` keeps dropping `headingLevel` for a non-`heading` split half. Only the block that was actually bulleted remembers"), and the paired lessons file (…-lessons.md:22-25) repeats the unqualified rule. docs/design/docs/docs.md:172-188 does document the exception, so the design-doc side is covered, but the plan's Non-goal was never amended, leaving the shipped behavior in direct conflict with the plan it was scoped by. No guard makes the code unreachable, the behavior is squarely in the design-fit lane (scope creep past a cited Non-goal plus unrequested CRDT surface), and the rubric grades "exceeds a stated Non-Goal" as major. The counter-argument (the Non-goal targets copying, while offset-0 moves) is a governance judgement, not a concrete refutation.

finding.summary: DOCX `<w:pStyle>` heading-level coercion is unrelated hardening, in an area the plan lists as a non-goal
finding.evidence: The plan's Non-goals include "DOCX/PPTX export of a bulleted heading's `pStyle`", and the diff nonetheless edits `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` to `Number()`/`trunc`/clamp the level plus three new tests, motivated by clipboard-injection hardening rather than by the un-list regression. It also duplicates a clamp that already exists for the same value in `packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:108` (`Math.min(6, Math.max(1, block.headingLevel ?? 1))`) — a shared `clampHeadingLevel` (one already exists in `serialize/markdown.ts`) would be the reuse-friendly home.

verdict.reason: All elements of the finding verify against the tree. packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:95-103 contains the new heading-level coercion (`Math.min(6, Math.max(1, Math.trunc(Number(headingLevel)) || 1))`) with an inline comment explicitly motivating it as XML-attribute-injection hardening against "untrusted input (the internal clipboard payload, DOCX/HTML/PPTX imports)" — unrelated to the un-list regression the plan describes. The three corresponding tests exist at packages/docs/test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts:101-115 (42→Heading6, 2.7→Heading2, -3→Heading1) with the same injection-hardening rationale in their comment. The plan's Non-goals list at docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:58 states verbatim "DOCX/PPTX export of a bulleted heading's `pStyle`", while its Approach/Steps (lines 18-47) cover only `unlistedBlockType`, the two stores, `toggleList`, and `model/document.ts` — no DOCX export work is requested. The duplication claim also holds: the same 1–6 clamp for the same value already exists at packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:108 and as a named helper `clampHeadingLevel` at packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:128-132, so the new inline clamp is a third copy in the same package. This is scope creep past an explicitly stated Non-Goal plus duplication of an existing helper — both `major` under this lens's rubric. No guard renders it unreachable, and the complaint is about whether the change belongs at all (design-fit), not a line-level correctness or security-specific judgement that would defer to another lens.
